chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you have prayed in the Masjid al-Shajara, say while you are seated at the end of the prayer, before you arise, what the one in Ihram would say. Then arise and walk until you reach the mile, and al-Bayda is level with you; so when it is level with you, then proclaim the Talbiyah.

key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءُ: Al-Bayda (The White One), a specific landmark or area used as a reference point for the miqat.
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in the state of Ihram (sacred pilgrimage attire/status).
key_terms.دُبُرِ الصَّلَاةِ: At the end of the prayer, immediately following the final salams.
key_terms.لَبِّهْ: Proclaim the Talbiyah (the specific invocation: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk...').
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajara (The Mosque of the Tree), a specific miqat location near Mecca.

ai.seo_question: What is the correct procedure for entering Ihram after praying at Masjid al-Shajara?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the precise ritual sequence for concluding the Ihram prayer at Masjid al-Shajara, emphasizing the recitation of the Ihram supplication while seated before standing. The pilgrim is then instructed to walk until reaching al-Bayda, a specific landmark, where the formal proclamation of the Talbiyah begins, marking the transition into the full state of Ihram. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on specific locations and timed supplications in Hajj rituals, linking physical movement with spiritual declaration.
